recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements—the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

rec7W1wTqYkkXHLsz.Bio: Topher Gardner hosts the BioCharisma Podcast, blending permaculture, alternative construction, and body work in his exploration of resilience and wellness.
rec7W1wTqYkkXHLsz.Name: Topher Gardner

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Flagpole As Forgotten Technology", "body": "Topher Gardner arrived with a theory he stumbled into while presenting on biochar at a conference where he was also talking about electroculture: that flagpoles are the leftovers of an antenna system. He described the conductive pole, the ornamental orb or fleur de lis on top, and a sheer flag carrying conductive filaments waving in humid air, which he argues would behave like a static field generator accumulating atmospheric charge. Chance Garton put an Egyptian hieroglyph on screen, pointing out that the glyph for neter, the word for god, gods or nature, is itself a flag. The Latin vexillum, rows and Ordo got pulled into the same picture."}, {"title": "Buildings That Were Really Machines", "body": "Topher Gardner contends that the grand old buildings we admire were closer to living machines than to decoration. He points to alcoves in old manors that he says were resistive heaters rather than fireplaces, later stuffed with wood once the electricity was gone, and to accounts of mantles with no carbon staining. As he put it, the level of consciousness that went into those buildings means you just wouldn't have an ornament for no reason. He carries that into his own build: a flagpole in a basalt footer so the ground current is not blocked, a Tesla pancake coil at the terminus, and biochar in the walls for EMF blocking."}, {"title": "Kyle's Endocrine Enneagram Board", "body": "Kyle Denton screen shared what he called his endocrinium gram, a hand drawn enneagram layered over the pentagon calendar Topher Gardner has been working out from his podcast conversation with Tom Sherman. He mapped the three ayurvedic doshas onto the nine stations, kapha at nine as the body and the balancer, pitta at three as the achiever, vata at six as mind and nerves, then placed glands at each point: thyroid at two, thymus at four, pituitary at five, gonads at eight. Kyle described the doshas as a biological calendar, a childlike kapha beginning, working years in pitta, and a late vata sage stage."}, {"title": "Twelve Bands And The Plus One", "body": "Chance Garton brought in Eileen McKusick's biofield work, in particular the vertical bands she describes, five flowing upward, five flowing downward and two moving both ways, with a thirteenth now emerging. He noted that biofield tuning practitioners usually work the horizontal rows rather than these columns, and wondered aloud whether the field partly adheres to whatever mental scaffolding a person brings to it. That met the rule of Kalel, the plus one, framed on the stream as the difference between ordinal and cardinal counting, and Topher Gardner's argument that the observer keeps adding a pressure wave, so the divisions never really settle at twelve or thirteen."}, {"title": "The Zenith Of The Sun Is For Prayer", "body": "The last hour turned to the quality of light. Topher Gardner, drawing on a year of sungazing while living at eight degrees of latitude in the jungle, argues that eastern morning light is piercing while afternoon light is diminishing even at an identical angle, and that the tiredness he felt at midday was actually his mind switching off, which led him to treat the zenith as prayer time. He notes Islamic prayer times track that exact minute. Chance Garton laid the Chinese meridian clock beside it, and Kyle Denton matched it to the ayurvedic day, including the kapha stretch of the afternoon when everyone goes sleepy."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight we're bringing together the genius gentlemen Christopher Gardner (BioCharisma Podcast) and Kyle Denton (Tippecanoe Herbs). Join us for a free form hangout with these extraordinarily wise guys, ask questions in the chat, and prepare for spontaneous enlightenment!
